title: Booking a seat when many people want the same one

hook.shape: Several contenders reach for one scarce seat at the same moment while a cited peak-demand figure lands, so the winner is unknown.

arc: contention → ordered steps with a tracker → two-clock trap → real-world payoff → pull-back over the whole board

beats.summary: Many contenders reach for the same single seat at the same instant, and a cited figure shows how busy that moment is.
A tap becomes traffic that travels the roads to a nearby cache and content network before any server sees it.
Every request passes one entry point that checks who the person is before anything else runs.
Search reads a separate copy of availability refreshed only now and then, so a listing flips to sold out while a screen still shows it free.
The venue's own system turns out to be the source of truth, and several venues with different interfaces feed one aggregator that outputs a single format.
A tap claims the seat under a hold that will expire, and a second request arriving moments later is turned away.
A user timer and the venue's hold timer run side by side, and the hold runs out just as a late payment clears, so the money is returned.
A queue feeds workers that build a confirmation, a scannable code and a ticket, and a person scans it at the gate where the record matches.
The camera pulls back over every part built so far, then closes with a short call to follow.

pacing: The hook stacks contenders quickly, then the roadmap slows down to name each step before any detail.
One board persists and grows, so each step adds a part instead of starting from scratch.
The two-clock beat sits longest on screen; the final pull-back is one uninterrupted move.
